html:
A road and rail bridge about 6 kilometres long across the Padma river, the main channel of the Ganges in Bangladesh. It opened on 25 June 2022, linking the less developed southwest of the country directly to the capital, Dhaka.

The Padma is wide, deep and fast, with shifting sandbanks, and its bed is soft silt. Until the bridge, travellers and lorries waited hours, sometimes days, for ferries, and ferry accidents were common. Building piers deep enough into the riverbed was one of the hardest engineering jobs of its kind.

The World Bank had agreed to lend money, but in 2012 it pulled out over claims of a corruption plot, claims that a Canadian court later threw out. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina then decided that Bangladesh would pay for the bridge with its own funds. A Chinese company built the main bridge. Its opening was celebrated as a sign of national confidence, half a century after the Liberation War. The rail link across it opened in 2023 and 2024.
